correctness.rationale: Edge-girth=4 equivalent to triangle-free plus every edge in some square. m<=3 impossible; if m=5, a first C4 plus a fifth edge must require a distinct C4 sharing at least three edges of first, impossible in a simple graph. Mantel triangle-free m<=floor(n²/4) yields n>=ceil(2sqrt m). For m>=7 put n=ceil(2sqrt m), a=floor(n/2),b=ceil(n/2),d=ab−m: n>=6, a,b>=3 and 0<=d<=a−1 using strict minimality of n. Delete a d-edge matching. Each surviving uv has opposite candidate neighbors of sizes >=a−2,>=b−2. If there is no square through uv, the entire candidate cross product is deleted matching, so each set has size one; this forces a=b=3 and three distinct missing edges, impossible since d<=2. Every same-side vertex pair shares a neighbor, proving connectivity. C4 and K2,3 handle m=4,6. An independent graph-construction check verified edge count, connectedness, no triangles and square coverage for 4 and every m=6..300, while analytic argument proves all m.

value.rationale: Solves the explicit vertex-count realization gap raised by the primary edge-girth-sequence paper in a natural whole-parameter class. Sharp n=ceil(2sqrt m), all forbidden m, and uniform constructive matching-deletion proof are nontrivial as square-coverage is stronger than Mantel's triangle-free density constraint; useful for extremal realization benchmarks.

final_claim: For a positive integer edge count m, the minimum order of a connected simple graph in which every edge lies on a 4-cycle but no triangles exist is infinity at m=1,2,3,5, and ceil(2 sqrt(m)) at m=4 or m>=6; balanced K_{a,b} with at most a−1 matching edges deleted realizes each admissible order.
limitations: Finite connected simple graphs only; minimum order, not all feasible orders, all isomorphism classes or diameter.
Numerical checks bounded at m<=300 and do not prove all m.
